Consider f_n as a function on all real numbers x. Determine all real x values at which f_n(x) is globally maximal, and determine the corresponding maximal value M(n) = max over real x of f_n(x).

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n>1 and every real t with 1 - 1/n <= t < 1, for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n we have floor(k*t) = k - 1; therefore (by the definition of f_n and H_n used in the surrounding context) f_n(t) equals H_n - 1 for all such t.

The final consequence f_n(t) = H_n - 1 is intended to depend on the fact that floor(k*t) equals k - 1 for all integers k in 1..n.

payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every real t with 1 - 1/n <= t < 1, one has floor(k*t) = k - 1 for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n; consequently, f_n(t) = H_n - 1.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1 and a real number t with 1 - 1/n <= t < 1. Let k be any integer with 1 <= k <= n.

First, since t < 1, we have kt < k. Hence floor(kt) <= k - 1.

Second, since t >= 1 - 1/n, we have
kt >= k(1 - 1/n) = k - k/n.
Because k <= n, we have k/n <= 1, so k - k/n >= k - 1. Therefore kt >= k - 1, and so floor(kt) >= k - 1.

Combining the two inequalities gives floor(kt) = k - 1 for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n.

Now evaluate f_n(t) using its definition:
f_n(t) = floor(nt) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kt)/k.
Since the above equality also holds for k=n, we have floor(nt)=n-1, and for every k,
floor(kt)/k = (k-1)/k = 1 - 1/k.
Thus
f_n(t) = (n-1) - sum_{k=1}^n (k-1)/k
        = (n-1) - sum_{k=1}^n (1 - 1/k)
        = (n-1) - (n - H_n)
        = H_n - 1,
where H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k is the nth harmonic number.

This proves the lemma.
result_payload.proof_summary: For t in [1-1/n,1), every kt with 1<=k<=n lies in [k-1,k), so floor(kt)=k-1. Substituting into the definition of f_n gives f_n(t)=H_n-1.

used_external_facts: standard floor-function inequalities: a<=y<a+1 iff floor(y)=a
